description: Somos Aether, un equipo del IES Guadalquivir (Lora del Río, Sevilla), apasionado por la ciencia, la tecnología y la innovación.
summary: First, you choose a character inspired by real astronauts who have participated in previous missions. Once chosen, a description of the character will appear. Then, you'll have to select the items your budget allows against the clock (30 seconds), and you'll be ready for launch. In space, you'll have to destroy space debris, and once finished, you can travel to the planet/satellite allowed by the level. There, you'll learn something about the celestial body and have to complete a few missions. When you finish, you'll be ready to return to Earth.
details:
Project Description

Our project involves developing an educational video game that aims to introduce the world of space exploration to people of all ages in an interactive, entertaining, and accessible way. Through Aether, an experience inspired by real space missions, players can learn more about how space travel is prepared and carried out, as well as the different challenges astronauts face.

The video game allows players to choose a character inspired by real astronauts, select the necessary equipment within a limited budget, launch a space mission, and complete various tasks. Among its main objectives are the identification and removal of space debris, as well as the exploration of planets and moons, where players can discover scientific information and complete activities related to each celestial body.

One of the project's main benefits is its ability to convey scientific knowledge in a practical and fun way. We want to spark curiosity about science, technology, and space exploration, especially among young people, while also appealing to adults and seniors who want to learn.Impact and Awareness

Our mission is to change society's perception of space expeditions. Many people associate space exploration solely with rocket launches, astronauts, or trips to the Moon. However, behind these journeys lie numerous scientific and technological challenges that we also need to understand.

One of the problems we want to highlight is the accumulation of space debris: defunct satellites, rocket fragments, and other remnants that remain in orbit. These objects can cause collisions and endanger future space missions. Furthermore, some fragments can fall back into Earth's atmosphere. Through this video game, we aim to raise awareness about the importance of keeping space safe and sustainable.

Technological Development

To develop our project, we used Scratch, a programming platform that allows us to create video games and interactive experiences using blocks of code. Thanks to this tool, we were able to design the characters, the space settings, the game mechanics, and the different missions.

We opted for a simple and fun tool that allowed us to transform an educational idea into an interactive experience.

Creativity and Innovation

The creativity of our project lies in combining scientific learning with the fun of a video game. We have designed it for people of different generations, from young people to adults and seniors, so that anyone can discover and learn about space without needing any prior scientific knowledge.

We also don't want players to be mere spectators, but rather to actively participate in missions, make decisions, manage their resources, and face different challenges. In this way, learning becomes a practical and entertaining experience.

Work Process and Decision-Making

During the development of the project, we followed a work process based on problem-solving and cooperation, using the Lombard method.

First, we analyzed and understood the problem we wanted to address. Then, we carried out an ideation phase in which we proposed different solutions and evaluated which one could be most effective.

Once we selected our idea, we sought to validate it by consulting both experts and people with no prior knowledge of the subject. We listened to their opinions, received suggestions, and made the necessary adjustments to improve our proposal. Finally, we managed to define an idea that combines education, technology, creativity, and environmental awareness, because we are convinced that the future depends not only on what we are capable of creating, but on how we decide to use it.
